policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the lemma as 'the high places of the earth,' which distinguishes the qere reading represented by r00-base.
ASV's wording 'I will go stripped and naked' renders the qere reading represented by r00-base.
ASV's main text has the first-person wording 'have I rolled myself in the dust,' distinguishing the ketiv r01; the mapped textual-variant note identifies 'roll thyself' as the other reading.
